events.title: The Pony Express Rides Out
events.description: The first successful Pony Express run began in Saint Joseph, Missouri. Riders carried mail by relay toward Sacramento, California, and the first trip finished later in April.
events.significance: The Pony Express became a lasting symbol of the American frontier. It sharply cut mail delivery times across the continent until the telegraph made it obsolete.

events.title: Outlaw Jesse James Is Killed
events.description: In St. Joseph, Missouri, Robert Ford shot and killed Jesse James, who was living under an assumed name. Ford was after a $5,000 reward.
events.significance: The death of one of the best-known outlaws of the American Old West turned James into a figure of folklore. Books, songs and films have retold his story ever since.

events.title: Truman Signs the Marshall Plan
events.description: President Harry S. Truman signed the Marshall Plan into law. It provided American economic aid to help rebuild Western European countries after World War II.
events.significance: The program helped revive war-torn economies and strengthened ties between the United States and Western Europe. It became a cornerstone of early Cold War policy.

events.title: The First Public Mobile Phone Call
events.description: Motorola engineer Martin Cooper placed the first public call from a handheld mobile phone, standing on a Manhattan sidewalk. He called Joel Engel, a rival researcher at Bell Labs.
events.significance: The call marked the start of the mobile phone era. Handheld phones have since reshaped how people communicate around the world.
